claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by removing Co.
The solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has a homogeneous atomic distribution.
Removing Co changes the degree and nature of lattice distortion in FeNiCrMn.
Removing Co modifies dislocation-core configurations through altered atomic-size mismatches and electronic interactions.
Edge-type dislocations are the primary dislocations governing the proposed behavior.
Co removal makes edge-dislocation mobility more sensitive to temperature and strain rate.
At low temperature and low strain rate, lattice distortion restricts edge-dislocation motion and raises strength.
At elevated temperature and/or higher strain rate, modified dislocation cores have reduced intrinsic friction.
Reduced dislocation friction at elevated temperature and/or higher strain rate enhances dislocation mobility and ductility.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show a steeper decline in yield strength as temperature increases.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have greater ductility at elevated temperatures.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have greater ductility at higher strain rates.
Co removal will shift the dominant dislocation activity observable by TEM and neutron diffraction.
The Co-containing CoCrFeMnNi baseline has more uniform and less temperature-sensitive dislocation behavior.
The Co-containing baseline commonly deforms by edge-dislocation activity.
Room-temperature-to-900°C compression at approximately 1 × 10^-4 s^-1 can be combined with in situ neutron diffraction to monitor deformation.
Outside room temperature to approximately 900°C and strain rates near 1 × 10^-4 s^-1, mechanisms such as twinning or creep may dominate.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis invokes systematic strain-rate variation and predicts behavior at higher strain rates, but the boundary restricts applicability to rates near 1 × 10^-4 s^-1 and the falsification experiment specifies only approximately 1 × 10^-4 s^-1. The proposed experiment therefore cannot test the strain-rate-dependent prediction.

The stated intervention is variation of temperature and strain rate, whereas the structural mediator is said to be induced by Co removal. Co removal is not represented as the controlled intervention linking the baseline to the mediator.
